reasoning: The fix follows the CLAUDE.md rule "Never build a user-facing sentence inside a wire type; emit structure and let the localized view render it". Core/Models/VendorNotice.swift adds two closed enums, VendorDisclaimer and VendorGuidance (Sendable, Codable, CaseIterable), with no [String: Any]. The App maps them to localized text in one place, App/Localization/VendorNoticeText.swift:38-68, and the switches are exhaustive with no default. So a new case fails to compile until it has a key, and VendorNoticeLocalizationTests.keys_exist_in_every_language checks that every key exists in en, pt-BR and es. AppError gains a single computed httpStatus (AppError.swift:41-58). isTransient, isRateLimited and isUnauthorized now read from it, which removes two `if case .http` pattern matches instead of adding a third. No error is swallowed: every throw site in AntigravityExecutor.swift, GeminiProvider.swift and XAIProvider.swift still throws, now as .guidance. CachedFetch.swift:54-58 keeps the status through `appErr.httpStatus ?? 0`; that is not a silent default, because the old code already used 0 there. New tests use expectTrue for optional conditions, as the Testing policy requires (e.g. GeminiXAILocaleNeutralTests `snap?.isAntigravityActive == true`). The two test names made stale by the fix were renamed (GeminiProviderTests `...throws antigravityNotFound guidance`, `...into structured guidance`). README and all three Localizable.strings were updated together. The report records validate exit 0 with 0 warnings; I did not rebuild, per the read-only protocol.
